fields.v: Zhu, J., Wu, J., Hu, M., Zhu, S., Pan, J., Shen, W., Yang, Y., Liu, F., Hao, J., Jin, Y., Ho, Q., Xu, M. (2026). SWE Context Bench: A Benchmark for Context Learning in Coding. arXiv:2602.08316v3 [cs.SE], 6 May 2026
Preprint — arXiv:2602.08316v3, marked 'Preprint'; no published venue stated (access log: arXiv record)

Mostly academia: University of Oxford, University of Edinburgh, TU Munich, National University of Singapore, MBZUAI, Carnegie Mellon University; one independent researcher; industry: MemoraX AI (one author, J. Hao)

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — benchmark SWE-ContextBench (and Lite) for cross-task context learning; compares five coding agents with/without oracle summaries, five context-reuse settings and memory retrieval frameworks

No SDD approach. Context-reuse settings: No-Context (baseline), Free Context Learning, Oracle Context Learning, Free Summary Learning, Oracle Summary Learning; memory retrieval frameworks: Mem0, OpenViking, LangMem, Supermemory (no versions)

Context pool of prior agent trajectories (tool calls, file navigation, reasoning) from 1,100 experience tasks; summary context pool (final summary paragraph of each trajectory, avg 217.1 tokens vs 25,633.7 for full trajectories); memories extracted/indexed by memory frameworks

Benchmark: run base agent (Claude Code + Sonnet 4.5) on experience tasks -> store trajectories -> for each related task, agent receives repo, base commit, problem statement (+ retrieved or oracle context depending on setting) -> generates patch -> FAIL_TO_PASS / PASS_TO_PASS evaluation
None in agent runs; related task instances identified and verified manually by the authors
Single artefact type (prior-experience context/memory given to the agent); no spec workflow
Not classifiable (context reuse/memory, not specifications)
Existing code bases: bug fixing of real GitHub issues (SWE-bench-derived)
1,476 tasks (1,100 experience + 376 related) from 51 repositories, 9 languages; Lite: 300 + 99 tasks, 12 Python repos; related tasks avg 4.8 FAIL_TO_PASS and 211.5 PASS_TO_PASS tests

Criterion: task resolved (FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS pass). Verdicts judged on each configuration's own values; the study sets no threshold. Quality: every configuration resolves a minority of tasks (16-34%) with few regressions (PASS_TO_PASS task level 86-90% on Lite) -> partly. Cost: every configuration costs under 1 USD and about 4-13 min per task -> works. Study 1 (SWE-ContextBench related tasks; 376 implied, the resolved % are multiples of 1/376), resolved % / avg cost USD / avg time s: (1) Claude Code + Claude Sonnet 4.5, baseline (no context): 19.68 / 0.67 / 344.47 (quality partly, cost works); (2) Claude Code + Claude Sonnet 4.5, oracle summary: 23.40 / 0.55 / 280.62 (partly, works); (3) Codex + GPT-5.3 Codex, baseline: 22.60 / 0.31 / 349.41 (partly, works); (4) Codex + GPT-5.3 Codex, oracle summary: 23.94 / 0.27 / 362.39 (partly, works); (5) Qwen Code + Qwen3.5-plus, baseline: 16.22 / 0.33 / 523.47 (partly, works); (6) Qwen Code + Qwen3.5-plus, oracle summary: 21.54 / 0.18 / 455.18 (partly, works); (7) Qwen Code + GLM-5, baseline: 18.35 / 0.58 / 800.99 (partly, works); (8) Qwen Code + GLM-5, oracle summary: 19.41 / 0.48 / 629.34 (partly, works); (9) Claude Code + MiniMax 2.7, baseline: 19.68 / 0.65 / 691.28 (partly, works); (10) Claude Code + MiniMax 2.7, oracle summary: 22.07 / 0.46 / 420.92 (partly, works). Study 2 (SWE-ContextBench Lite, 99 related tasks; Claude Sonnet 4.5, agent not stated), resolved % / time min / cost USD: (11) No-Context (baseline): 26.26 / 6.37 / 0.79 (partly, works); (12) Free Context Learning: 26.26 / 6.78 / 0.98 (partly, works); (13) Oracle Context Learning: 27.27 / 5.95 / 0.77 (partly, works); (14) Free Summary Learning: 22.22 / 6.28 / 0.91 (partly, works); (15) Oracle Summary Learning: 34.34 / 6.66 / 0.85 (partly, works); (16) Mem0: 24.24 / 4.72 / 0.62, ingestion of 300 trajectories about 21 min, 0.24 USD (partly, works); (17) OpenViking: 29.20 / 4.20 / 0.53, ingestion about 570 min, 18.96 USD (partly, works); (18) Supermemory: 30.30 / 5.04 / 0.58, ingestion 369.6k tokens, under 1 h (partly, works); (19) LangMem: no resolution or run cost reported, only retrieval match (73.34% overall) and ingestion (about 58 min, 0.98 USD): quality and cost not assessable
fields.why: Section 6 requires a verdict for every configuration, baseline included, judged on its own: r1 gave no verdict to the baselines of Study 1 and Study 2, gave one pooled verdict to the five oracle-summary configurations, and justified the Study 2 verdicts by the difference from the baseline. Values unchanged (re-checked against Tables 3 and 4); times, ingestion costs and one entry per configuration added. The absolute cut-off is a judgement: a stricter reader could rate the configurations under 20% resolved (5, 7, 8, 1, 9) as does not work

fields.v: Study 1: 5 agent+model configurations x {baseline, oracle summary}. Study 2: Claude Sonnet 4.5 x 5 context settings on 99 Lite tasks (495 runs) + memory frameworks. Baseline: No-Context. Held constant: task prompt template (repo, base commit, problem statement), fresh isolated environment, git history removed, no state carryover. Acceptance tests: FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS from the PR test patch. Repetitions: not stated (apparently one run per task). Human intervention: none

Oracle summaries improved resolution for all five agents (+1.1 to +5.3 points) and lowered cost; best GPT-5.3 Codex 23.94%. On Lite: Oracle Summary best resolution (34.34% vs 26.26%, +8.08); Oracle Context lowest time and cost (5.95 min, 0.77 USD); Free Context most expensive (0.98 USD, +27.3% over Oracle Context, about +24% over the baseline) with no gain in resolution; Free Summary below baseline (22.22%); both summary settings cost more than baseline on Lite (0.91, 0.85 vs 0.79 USD); Supermemory best framework (30.30%), OpenViking cheapest and fastest (0.53 USD, 4.20 min). No significance tests despite 'significantly improve' in the abstract
fields.why: The 27.3% increase in the text (p. 8) is Free Context (0.98) relative to Oracle Context (0.77), not relative to the baseline (0.79, which gives about 24%); r1 left the reference ambiguous

fields.v: Distinguished oracle vs free context and frameworks on resolution and cost. Repeatability: single runs, no variance reported; prompt template given. Limitations stated: no comprehensive human validation of problem statements, test patches or solvability; context pool quality not filtered (noisy trajectories)

Context helps only when compact and correctly selected; free retrieval can hurt. Gaps: summarization quality, structured context management, adaptive decisions on when to reuse, adaptive retrieval, critical use of retrieved context; limitation: lack of human validation of tasks

Tables 3, 4 and 5 jumbled by pdftotext; values rebuilt by column order and cross-checked with text (e.g. GPT-5.3 Codex 22.60/23.94, Claude 23.40, Oracle Summary 34.34, costs 0.77/0.98/0.79/0.91/0.85); Table 3 resolved rates are all multiples of 1/376, supporting the 376 related tasks as its task set. Table 4 includes Mem0, OpenViking, Supermemory only, although the text says it compares four frameworks (LangMem missing). OpenViking's 29.20% resolved on 99 tasks is not a possible value (k/99 gives 29.29), likely a typo. Task set for Table 3 (376 related vs other) is not stated explicitly. Agent for Study 2 not restated (only Claude Sonnet 4.5). Abstract claims 'significantly' without statistical tests, and says summarized experience reduces token cost, while on Lite summary reuse cost more than the baseline (p. 8). Text says oracle summaries improve 'most models' while Table 3 shows all five improve. Name misspelled 'SWE-ContxetBench' in headings. Benchmark said to be released (Lite) but no URL in the text. No pre-registration. Languages: 9 (Python dominant)
fields.why: Added a reporting inconsistency: OpenViking 29.20% resolved cannot occur on 99 tasks (29/99 = 29.29%); and noted that the Table 3 rates fit a 376-task denominator
